subject: Mid-Q steering: prioritize scope trims and assign dependency owners

From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Eli Crawford <eli@somnusanalytics.com>

Subject: Mid-Q steering: prioritize scope trims and assign dependency owners

Team —

Quick mid-quarter pulse before the Friday steer: attached is a one-page heatmap (MIDQ_OKR_Heatmap.pdf) that synthesizes progress against the product and go-to-market OKRs. High level:
- Product Serving Runtime (OKR-1): 58% complete — major infra blockers on live-traffic KV cache (yellow).
- Model Catalog & Rollouts (OKR-2): 72% complete — dependent on policy gating work from Security (green/yellow).
- Cost Optimization (OKR-3): 40% — deferred until quantization work lands (red).

We need to:
1) Agree which sub-initiatives we trim to protect QBR commitments (my recommendation: postpone non-critical A/B experiments in OKR-3; keep the model-variant caching work).
2) Assign clear dependency owners and due dates — see the attached Dependency_Roster_V2.csv.
3) Confirm a small runway request for infra time (2 GPU-weeks) for the KV cache unblock.

Eli — I'm looping you in because Somnus is asking for the model-variant fallback we promised on the November milestone; we should align scope so we don't over-promise.

Asks:
- Naomi: can you confirm which commercial commitments we must keep at full scope vs which can be trimmed?
- Markus: can you sign off on scope trim principle (A) defer experimentation, (B) keep all SLA-facing items?
- Karthik: can you surface the blocker list and whether 2 GPU-weeks is sufficient?

Thanks — short replies are fine; we can synthesize for the steer meeting.

Mina Haddad
Head of Product Operations | Redwood Inference

Mina / Naomi —

Quick technical status on KV cache unblock: summary and ask:
- Root cause: a race when evicting prefix entries under heavy concurrent streaming; repro rate ~12% at seq_len=4096 in canary.
- Current mitigation: reduced concurrency and trimmed batch sizes (latency cost increase ~8%) — not acceptable long-term.
- Work required: kernel patch + integration test + 1 week of on-rack validation under traffic patterns (~2 GPU-weeks total).

I confirm 2 GPU-weeks is the right ask if we prioritize it now. I'll push an RFC to the infra queue today and link SUP-289. Short timeline: patch by 09/10, integration 09/13-09/16, validation 09/17.

Related notes: if we defer KV fixes, we should lower the target throughput for the hosted plan during the fallback window (Naomi, that will change the SLA wording we send to Somnus).

Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-289

Karthik Iyer
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
Attachment: SUP-289-playbook.md (md stub)

- Approve the 2 GPU-weeks runway for KV cache fix; Karthik to proceed with RFC and SUP-289 as the tracking ticket.
- Naomi to own the Somnus deliverable; align messaging with legal/solutions (deadline 2026-10-01).
